properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 6 at 12:23PM MDT until September 7 at 12:00AM MDT by NWS Salt Lake City UT
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of Utah, including the following areas, Central
Mountains, Eastern Juab/Millard Counties, Sanpete Valley, Sevier
Valley, Wasatch Plateau/Book Cliffs, Western Uinta Basin, Bryce
Canyon Country, South Central Utah, Southern Mountains, Upper
Sevier River Valleys, Southwest Utah and Zion National Park. This
watch also includes recent burn scars such as Cottonwood, Widemouth
2, Forsyth, France Canyon, Monroe Canyon, and Black Canyon.

* WHEN...Until midnight MDT tonight.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, dry washes, slot canyons, and other low-lying and
flood-prone locations such as slickrock areas and recent burn
scars.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Excessive rainfall is expected Sunday afternoon associated with
the arrival of deep tropical moisture across much of central and
southern Utah. Rates from 0.1-0.3 inches per hour are expected,
with isolated higher rates possible.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.

NWSheadline: FLOOD WATCH REMAINS IN EFFECT UNTIL MIDNIGHT MDT TONIGHT

properties.areaDesc: East Glacier Park Region; Northern High Plains; Eastern Glacier, Western Toole, and Central Pondera; Eastern Toole and Liberty; Southern Rocky Mountain Front; Southern High Plains; Eastern Pondera and Eastern Teton
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 6 at 11:32AM MDT until September 8 at 12:00PM MDT by NWS Great Falls MT
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHERE...A portion of north central Montana, including the following
areas, East Glacier Park Region, Eastern Glacier, Western Toole,
and Central Pondera, Eastern Pondera and Eastern Teton, Eastern
Toole and Liberty, Northern High Plains, Southern High Plains and
Southern Rocky Mountain Front.

* WHEN...From 3 PM MDT this afternoon through Tuesday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in minor flooding of creeks,
streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations. Creeks and
streams may rise out of their banks. Flooding may occur in poor
drainage areas. Rural gravel and dirt roads can become muddy and
may become difficult to travel. Rock/debris slides are possible in
the mountains.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Thunderstorms today will be capable of producing 0.50 to 1 inch
per hour rain rates. Periods of moderate to heavy rainfall will
be possible Monday through Tuesday morning. Widespread 0.75 to
1.5 inches of rain have already fallen along the Rocky Mountain
Front over the past 24 hours. Additional widespread rain
accumulations of 1 to 3 inches are possible along the Rocky
Mountain Front and Sweet Grass Hills with isolated 4 inches
possible along and north of US Highway 2 this afternoon through
Tuesday morning.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be alert for possible Flood
Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible.

* WHEN...From 3 PM MDT this afternoon through Tuesday morning.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of creeks,
streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations. Creeks and
streams may rise out of their banks. Flooding may occur in poor
drainage and urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Thunderstorms capable of rainfall rates of 0.75" to 1.00" per
hour are possible this afternoon and evening (Sept 6), which
could lead to localized debris flows.

This period will then be followed by prolonged moderate to heavy
rainfall Monday into Tuesday morning of an additional 1 to 3
inches in the valleys, with 2 to 4 inches in the higher terrain,
especially along the Continental Divide and in Glacier National
Park.

properties.areaDesc: Niihau; Kauai Southwest; Kauai Mountains; Kauai North; Kauai East; Kauai South
properties.headline: Flood Watch issued September 6 at 4:15AM HST until September 8 at 6:00PM HST by NWS Honolulu HI
properties.description:
Moisture along the eastern flank of Hurricane Lowell will bring
periods of heavy rain to the main Hawaiian Islands late Sunday
through Tuesday.

* WHAT...Flash flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...Kauai and Niihau.

* WHEN...From noon HST today through Tuesday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Significant flooding may occur due to the overflow of
streams and drainages. Roads in several areas may be closed, along
with property damage in urban or low lying spots due to runoff.
Landslides may also occur in areas with steep terrain.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Moisture along the eastern flank of Hurricane Lowell will bring
periods of heavy rain to the main Hawaiian islands late Sunday
through Tuesday. Initially, the threat of heavy rain will be
highest along windward and mountain areas, then the threat will
spread everywhere as the winds become more southerly by Monday.
- Kauai and Niihau.
properties.instruction:
You should monitor later forecasts and be prepared to take action
should Flash Flood Warnings be issued.
